title: Microsoft Purview: Data Loss Prevention now covers Microsoft Cowork
summary: The briefing passes: the automatic extension of existing policies, rollout dates, controls and documented Cowork limitations are supported. The cost rationale should replace its loose E5-tier shorthand with a reference to the exact licensing plans already listed in the briefing.

claims.claim: Learn documents one policy location named Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork.

claims.claim: The notice limits prompt DLP to prompt text, excluding uploaded files at this time.

claims.quote: Customizing the link in Copilot policy tips isn't yet supported for Cowork.

claims.quote: This feature is in preview and is rolling out to all tenants with access to Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat. Check whether rollout has reached your tenant. Cowork supports this feature

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Sensitivity-label rules prevent Copilot and Cowork from using matching file and email content in responses.
claims.quote: Copilot and Cowork don't process the content of the item or use it in the response summary, but the item could be available in the citations of the response.

claims.claim: Items identified by sensitivity-label rules can still appear in response citations.
claims.quote: Identified items still appear in the citations of the response, but Copilot and Cowork don't access or use the content of the item in the response.

claims.claim: Sensitivity-label protection supports file items.
claims.quote: File items, which are stored and items that are actively open.

claims.claim: Sensitivity-label email protection covers emails sent on or after January 1, 2025.
claims.quote: Emails sent on or after January 1, 2025.

claims.claim: Calendar invites are not supported by this sensitivity-label protection.
claims.quote: Calendar invites aren't supported.

claims.where: Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Learn says DLP checks typed prompt text rather than scanning the contents of files uploaded directly into prompts.
claims.quote: DLP can't scan the contents of files that you upload directly into prompts, so evaluation of the uploaded file for sensitive data doesn't occur. DLP only checks the text you type into the prompt itself.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot prompts run in the submitting user's security context.
claims.quote: All Microsoft 365 Copilot prompts run in the security context of the user who initiates the prompt.

claims.claim: Users must already have permission to access content before seeing it in a prompt response.
claims.quote: This means for a user to see an item in a prompt response, they must first have the necessary permissions to access the content of the item.

claims.claim: DLP can exclude items from response processing in addition to the user's existing access permissions.
claims.quote: You can then use the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork policy location feature to exclude items from being processed in the response summary.

claims.claim: Policy simulation mode is available for Microsoft 365 Copilot and Cowork.
claims.quote: Policy simulation mode is available for Microsoft 365 Copilot and Cowork.

claims.quote: DLP policy scoping for Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Cowork is based on the user who submits the prompt, not the owner of a file or email that the experience accesses.

claims.claim: The Purview portal path is Data Loss Prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Custom > Custom policy > Locations > Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork.
claims.quote:
Go to Data Loss Prevention > Policies and select + Create policy.
Select the Custom template, then Custom policy.
On the Locations page, set the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork location to on.

claims.claim: New-DlpCompliancePolicy -Name "<policy name>" -Locations $loc -EnforcementPlanes @("CopilotExperiences") creates the policy at the Copilot location, as qualified in the note.
claims.quote: New-DLPCompliancePolicy -Name "Copilot Policy" -Locations $loc -EnforcementPlanes @("CopilotExperiences")

claims.claim: No separate Cowork switch at the combined DLP location is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Cowork DLP separate policy switch Copilot only Cowork exclude location. Read the feature page, including conditions/actions and admin units, and MC1477182; no workload-separation setting found.

claims.claim: DLP alerts are supported for the combined location that includes Cowork.
claims.quote: DLP alerts and DLP notifications are supported.

claims.claim: The PowerShell reference example configures the Microsoft 365 Copilot location with sensitivity labels.

claims.claim: The New-DlpCompliancePolicy reference page does not mention Cowork.
claims.quote: Searched: New-DlpCompliancePolicy EnforcementPlanes CopilotExperiences Cowork. Opened the cited command reference and searched its full text for Cowork and Copilot; the example and Locations parameter name Copilot, not Cowork.

claims.claim: The notice recommends informing compliance, security and AI governance stakeholders.

claims.claim: The cost rationale collectively describes the eligible file and email protection plans as E5-tier plans.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 E5/A5, Microsoft Purview Suite/EDU/FLW and Microsoft Defender + Purview Suite FLW, Microsoft 365 E5/A5/F5 Information Protection and Governance | Office 365 E5/A5
claims.fix: In the cost rationale, replace 'included only in E5-tier plans' with 'included in the plans listed in Cost and licensing'. This avoids treating the broad E5-tier shorthand as an exact licence requirement.

claims.claim: DLP notifications are supported for the combined location that includes Cowork.
claims.quote: DLP alerts and DLP notifications are supported.

claims.claim: A matching prompt-blocking rule prevents Cowork from returning a response to that prompt.
claims.quote: This policy prevents Copilot and Cowork from returning a response when prompts contain sensitive data.

claims.claim: A matching web-search rule blocks web search for that prompt rather than necessarily blocking the response.
claims.quote: When a user prompt contains the configured SITs, Copilot and Cowork block external web search as a grounding source and continue to generate the response using allowed internal Microsoft 365 data sources.

claims.claim: The DLP policy control can have tenant-wide scope.
claims.quote: An unrestricted administrator can scope policies to administrative units or keep Full directory to apply a policy across the organization. Existing tenant-wide policies continue to apply; using administrative units is optional.
